title: Require an independent pre-deployment bias audit for any AI-based hiring or screening tool
description: Illustrative reference decision, provided as seed content for the AI Governance Workbench schema and not a documented decision of any specific organisation. It models the kind of governance decision commonly recommended in response to incidents like the 2018 Amazon recruiting-tool case, and aligns with the approach mandated by NYC Local Law 144 for automated employment decision tools.
decision_statement: No AI-based tool that screens, scores, or ranks candidates for hiring, promotion, or termination may be deployed against live candidates until it has passed a documented bias audit, conducted by a party independent of the tool's developers, measuring selection-rate disparities across protected characteristics. The audit must be repeated whenever the model, training data, or scoring logic materially changes.
decision_context: Motivated by publicly reported cases of AI hiring tools developing discriminatory patterns from historical training data, and by the emergence of legal requirements (e.g. NYC Local Law 144) mandating independent bias audits for automated employment decision tools.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Talent Acquisition Technology Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Rely solely on post-deployment monitoring rather than a pre-deployment gate.
Permit internal (non-independent) audits to satisfy the requirement.
